svg.aria-label: Load Testing Lab architecture: a developer workstation with the ltlab CLI, a repository and a browser; a Docker host running k6, Artillery, Telegraf, InfluxDB, Grafana and a toy API on one bridge network; and an external API as an optional target
svg.title: Load Testing Lab architecture
svg.desc: Left, the developer workstation: browser, ltlab CLI and your repository. Center, the Docker host with the ltl-net bridge network: load generators k6 and Artillery, Telegraf on StatsD port 8125, InfluxDB 2.6 on port 8086 with the influxdb-data volume, Grafana 10.1 on port 3000 built from provisioning files with six dashboards, and the toy API on port 5000. Right, your own API outside the stack. Numbered arrows: 1 the CLI starts the stack; 2 it runs a scenario mounted read-only from your repository; 3 the generators send HTTP load to the toy API or your API; 4 k6 writes metrics to InfluxDB directly while Artillery goes through Telegraf; 5 Grafana queries InfluxDB in Flux; 6 you open the dashboards in the browser.
svg.text: Defaults from docker-compose.yml; ports are host:container. The numbers follow the flow in the legend.
ltlab start runs docker compose up -d --wait: the stack comes
up on the ltl-net bridge network, and the command returns once
ltlab k6 -s or ltlab artillery -s runs a scenario; a file or
folder from your repository is mounted read-only into the
The generators send HTTP load to TARGET_API_URL: the toy API
inside the network, or any API the lab can reach.
k6 writes its metrics straight to InfluxDB through
xk6-influxdb; Artillery sends StatsD to Telegraf, which writes
